message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"0143453b1902588bb95ce3ff3bc696432099677dd5b411961e37ada1872117c0","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-va-class-std:lineage:86","source_registry_sha256":"b6300aba50e85a8fd509daf2f853e3d2d116b38a9707baf75df5057c8071f937","units":[{"unit_id":"sec01-u01","module_id":"sec01-m01","objective_ids":["sec01-u01"],"title":{"text":"The two-part knowledge exam","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F02","sec01-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Virginia testing can include vision screening, a two-part knowledge exam and a road skills test, and a DMV representative tells you which apply.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01"]},{"text":"Part one is ten traffic sign questions that must all be right before part two opens, and part two passes at eighty percent.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R01"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Tomas sits the knowledge exam and answers nine of the ten traffic sign questions in part one correctly.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Part one requires all ten sign questions to be answered correctly before part two is allowed.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R01"]},"result":{"text":"Tomas does not move on to part two on this attempt.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking part one passes at eighty percent like part two.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"Part one needs a perfect ten for ten on traffic signs; only part two passes at eighty percent.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Signs perfect first, then eighty percent.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Tomas gets nine of ten sign questions right in part one. Can he start part two?","fact_ids":["sec01-F04"]},"answer":{"text":"No. Part one needs all ten sign questions right before part two is allowed.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R01"]},"rationale":{"text":"Part one is a perfect-score gate, and the eighty percent standard applies only to part two.","fact_ids":["sec01-R01","sec01-F05"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Three tests, one plan","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Vision screening.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},{"text":"Two-part knowledge exam.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},{"text":"Road skills test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the first lesson on Virginia testing. Virginia testing can include three things: a vision screening, a two-part knowledge exam, and a road skills test. You do not have to guess which of them apply to you, because a DMV representative tells each applicant which tests apply. In this lesson we focus on the knowledge exam: who has to take it, how it is delivered, what its two parts ask of you, and where you can find a sample exam to practice with. We will also note what to do if you have special needs or a disability and need help with your application or your testing.","fact_ids":["sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-F12","sec01-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who takes the knowledge exam","fact_ids":["sec01-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Required for most applicants.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02"]},{"text":"Exempt: valid license from another United States state.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02"]},{"text":"Also exempt: Canada, Germany, France, Republic of Korea.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Start with who must sit the knowledge exam. The rule is that you must take it, unless you hold a valid driver license from another United States state, from Canada, from Germany, from France, or from the Republic of Korea. So the exemption depends on the license you already hold, and it has to be valid. If your license is from somewhere outside that list, or you have never been licensed, the knowledge exam is part of your path. Keep this list in mind, because the road skills test has its own exemption list in a later lesson, and the two lists are not quite the same. Learn this one as five places: other states, Canada, Germany, France and Korea.","fact_ids":["sec01-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":48,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"How the exam is built","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Runs on a computer.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},{"text":"Covers signs, laws and safe driving.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},{"text":"Every question comes from this manual.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Next, how the exam is delivered. The two-part knowledge exam runs on a computer. It covers three areas: traffic signs, motor vehicle laws, and safe driving. And here is the reassuring part: every question is drawn from this manual. That means every question you meet comes from this manual, so studying the manual covers the exam's three areas. Part one holds ten traffic sign questions. Part two is general-knowledge multiple choice. The two parts are scored in very different ways, which is exactly where many applicants get confused, so the next slide sets the two standards side by side so that you never mix them up on exam day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F03","sec01-F04","sec01-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Part one is a gate","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Part one: all ten signs correct.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Part two: at least eighty percent.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Part two waits for part one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Many people assume both parts pass at the same mark. They do not. Part one holds ten traffic sign questions, and you must answer all ten correctly before part two is allowed. That is a perfect ten for ten. Part two is general-knowledge multiple choice, and passing it requires at least eighty percent correct. So part one is a gate with no room for a miss, and part two is where the eighty percent standard lives. If you remember only one thing from this lesson, remember the order and the two standards: perfect on signs first, then eighty percent on general knowledge.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-F05","sec01-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the gate","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R01","sec01-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Nine of ten signs right in part one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R01","sec01-F05"]},{"text":"May part two begin?","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R01","sec01-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Tomas sits the knowledge exam and answers nine of the ten traffic sign questions in part one correctly. Can he start part two? Work it out before reading on. The answer is no. Part one requires all ten sign questions to be answered correctly before part two is allowed, so nine out of ten does not open the second part. The eighty percent standard belongs only to part two, which is general-knowledge multiple choice. Part one is a perfect-score gate. If you answered yes because nine out of ten sounds like a strong score, that is the exact confusion this lesson is designed to clear up for you.","fact_ids":["sec01-F04","sec01-R01","sec01-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Practice and support","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Sample exam: Section eight and DMV website.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-R01"]},{"text":"Special needs: tell DMV staff.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, two practical points. A sample knowledge exam appears in Section eight of this manual and on the DMV website, so you can practice in the same format before your attempt. And if you have special needs or a disability, tell DMV staff at any location when you need help with your application or your testing. To recap the lesson: Virginia testing can include vision screening, a two-part knowledge exam and a road skills test, and DMV tells you which apply. The knowledge exam runs on a computer, every question comes from the manual, part one needs all ten signs right, and part two passes at eighty percent.","fact_ids":["sec01-F12","sec01-F13","sec01-F01","sec01-F03","sec01-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u02","module_id":"sec01-m02","objective_ids":["sec01-u02"],"title":{"text":"Exam conduct, attempts and retakes","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R05","sec01-F11"]},"why_how":[{"text":"You get one knowledge exam attempt per business day, and help, sharing and phones are all banned while testing.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F11"]},{"text":"A minor who fails waits fifteen full days, and three failures mean a course before a fourth attempt.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-R02"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ava is seventeen and fails the knowledge exam on January one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A failing applicant under eighteen must wait a full fifteen days before retaking.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"result":{"text":"The earliest Ava can retake the exam is January seventeen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a translator can sit beside you whenever you ask for one.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"Translators are barred wherever the exam is offered in an audio version or a language version, including American Sign Language.","fact_ids":["sec01-R05","sec01-F07"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"One a day; qualify after three failures.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F08","sec01-R02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Ava, seventeen, fails the knowledge exam on January one. What is her earliest retake date?","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]},"answer":{"text":"January seventeen, because she must wait a full fifteen days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R02"]},"rationale":{"text":"A failing applicant under eighteen waits a full fifteen days, so failing on January one makes January seventeen the earliest retake.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Rules on exam day","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F06","sec01-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"One attempt per business day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F06","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"Language versions and translators.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F06","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"Waits and courses after failures.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F06","sec01-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on exam-day rules and what happens after a failure. The knowledge exam has a daily limit, a set of language options, and a clear list of things you may not do while testing. It also has different consequences depending on your age and on how many times you have failed. By the end of this lesson you should be able to answer three questions. How often may you try the knowledge exam? When are translators allowed? And what must happen before a retake, both for an applicant under eighteen after a single failure, and for any applicant after a third failure? Let us take these questions one at a time, starting with the daily limit.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F06","sec01-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":48,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Attempts and languages","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Only one attempt per business day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R05"]},{"text":"Audio version and many languages, including American Sign Language.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R05"]},{"text":"Translators barred where versions exist.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Only one knowledge exam attempt is allowed per business day. The exam also comes in an audio version and in many languages, including American Sign Language. Because those versions exist, translators are barred where those versions are offered. Put the two ideas together: the exam offers an audio version and many languages including American Sign Language, yet translators stay barred wherever those versions exist. Where an audio or language version is offered, that version is used and a translator is not. Expect this rule on the exam, because it is easy to assume that asking for a translator is always allowed when in fact the built-in versions replace one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Conduct while testing","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"No getting help.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"No helping another person.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"No seeking or sharing questions or answers.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},{"text":"No cell phone.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Now the conduct rules. While testing you may not get help, you may not help another person, you may not seek or share questions or answers, and you may not use a cell phone. Notice that receiving help and giving help are two separately banned acts. You cannot excuse helping a neighbor by saying you did not receive any help yourself. Seeking questions beforehand and sharing them afterward are banned as well, so the rule reaches before and after the exam, not only the moment you are seated at the computer. And the cell phone rule is simple: no phone use while testing. Treat all four of these as firm rules, because each one is listed separately.","fact_ids":["sec01-F11","sec01-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":47,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Retakes after failing","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Under eighteen: wait a full fifteen days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Fail January one, retake January seventeen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-R02"]},{"text":"Three failures: qualifying classroom or manual course.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"What happens after a failed attempt depends on your age and your count of failures. A failing applicant under age eighteen must wait a full fifteen days before retaking, and the manual gives an example: failing on January one means January seventeen is the earliest retake. After three failures, pass classroom driver education or an approved eight-hour manual course before a fourth attempt. Adults may take the manual course; minors need earlier classroom completion. Complete the manual course after the third failure and give DMV its certificate. Keep these two consequences apart, because the exam likes to swap them, and both involve a number you will need to recall.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The course path by age","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Eighteen or older: eight-hour manual course.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-R03"]},{"text":"Younger than eighteen: classroom driver education first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-R03"]},{"text":"Certificate goes to DMV, then retake.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap about the course option after a third failure. Drivers age eighteen or older may instead finish an eight-hour DMV-approved course based on this manual, taken after the third failure at a training school or online, and then retake after giving DMV the completion certificate. Drivers younger than eighteen may use that manual course only after finishing classroom driver education, and they must show the classroom certificate to the training school first. In short, after three failures adults may take the manual course directly, while minors may take it only after already completing classroom driver education. Do not assume the course path is the same for everyone.","fact_ids":["sec01-F09","sec01-F10","sec01-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the wait","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R02","sec01-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Ava is seventeen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R02","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"She fails on January one.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R02","sec01-F08"]},{"text":"Earliest retake date?","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R02","sec01-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Ava is seventeen and she fails the knowledge exam on January one. What is her earliest retake date? Work it out before reading on. The answer is January seventeen. A failing applicant under age eighteen must wait a full fifteen days before retaking, and the manual itself uses this example: failing on January one means January seventeen is the earliest retake. Notice that the wait is a full fifteen days, which is why the date lands on the seventeenth rather than the sixteenth. After a third failure, Ava needs classroom education or, if she already completed it, an approved eight-hour manual course completed after that failure with its certificate given to DMV.","fact_ids":["sec01-F06","sec01-R02","sec01-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Rules to carry","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F11","sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"One attempt a day, no translators where versions exist.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F11","sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},{"text":"No help, no sharing, no phone.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F11","sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},{"text":"Fifteen days for minors; course after three failures.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F11","sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us close the lesson. You get one knowledge exam attempt per business day. The exam comes in an audio version and many languages, including American Sign Language, so translators are barred where those versions are offered. While testing you may not get help, help anyone else, seek or share questions or answers, or use a cell phone. A failing applicant under eighteen waits a full fifteen days. After three failures, a fourth attempt requires the classroom part of driver education, and adults may instead take the eight-hour manual course, while minors may use it only after finishing classroom driver education. The memory line is: one a day, and three strikes means class.","fact_ids":["sec01-F07","sec01-F11","sec01-F06","sec01-F08","sec01-F09","sec01-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec01-u03","module_id":"sec01-m03","objective_ids":["sec01-u03"],"title":{"text":"The road skills test","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F16"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The road skills test is required unless your valid license is from a listed place, and Taiwan is on this list.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14"]},{"text":"You bring a legal, fully working test vehicle and one of two documents: a driver education certificate or the CSMA nineteen checklist.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-R06"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Omar, an adult permit holder, fails his first road skills test at DMV.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19"]},"reasoning":{"text":"The road test allows one attempt per business day, and after a failure you wait two days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08"]},"result":{"text":"Omar may try again after a two-day wait; only after three DMV failures would he need in-vehicle training first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking any vehicle will do for the road skills test as long as it runs.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15"]},"correction":{"text":"The vehicle cannot be an autocycle and must show a valid inspection sticker, plates, registration card and decals, plus working brakes, belts, horn, lights, signals, mirrors and speedometer.","fact_ids":["sec01-F15"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"One fail, two days; three fails, training.","fact_ids":["sec01-R08"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Omar fails his first road test at DMV. How long must he wait before trying again?","fact_ids":["sec01-F19"]},"answer":{"text":"Two days, since one road failure costs two waiting days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08"]},"rationale":{"text":"The road test allows one attempt per business day, and after a failure the wait is two days; the in-vehicle course applies only after three DMV failures.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Getting to the road test","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"Who must take it.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F19"]},{"text":"What you bring.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F19"]},{"text":"Where you test.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on the road skills test. Like the knowledge exam, the road skills test has an exemption list, and in this lesson we will compare the two lists. You will also learn what the test vehicle must have, which document the examiner needs to see before testing you, where applicants under eighteen take the test, what adults must do before their first attempt, and the waiting rules after a failure. The road test has its own retake pattern, and it is easy to confuse with the knowledge exam pattern from the last lesson, so pay attention to the numbers: two days after one failure, and a training course after three failures at DMV.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F16","sec01-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Exemptions and the vehicle","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Exempt: valid license from another state, Canada, Germany, France, Korea or Taiwan.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"You supply the vehicle; no autocycle.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F02"]},{"text":"Sticker, plates, registration card and decals.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"The road skills test is required unless you hold a valid license from another United States state, Canada, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea, or Taiwan. Compare that with the knowledge exam list: Taiwan appears only on the road skills list. Next, the vehicle. You must supply the test vehicle, and it cannot be an autocycle. It must show a valid inspection sticker, plates, a registration card and decals. It also needs working brakes, belts, a horn, lights, signals, mirrors and a speedometer. The vehicle is part of your test preparation, so check every one of these items before your appointment rather than discovering a problem at the test site.","fact_ids":["sec01-F14","sec01-F15","sec01-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The document you need","fact_ids":["sec01-F16","sec01-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Driver education completion certificate, or","fact_ids":["sec01-F16","sec01-R06"]},{"text":"Behind-the-wheel checklist on form CSMA nineteen.","fact_ids":["sec01-F16","sec01-R06"]},{"text":"One of the two is always required.","fact_ids":["sec01-F16","sec01-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Before testing you, the examiner requires a document. It can be an accepted driver education completion certificate, or a completed behind-the-wheel checklist on DMV form CSMA nineteen, with a licensed driver certifying your supervised practice and your compliance with the permit rules. In other words, the examiner accepts either the certificate or the checklist, and one of the two is always required. You never arrive with neither. If you learned through a driver education course, the certificate is your document. If you practiced with a licensed driver, the CSMA nineteen checklist, certified by that driver, is the document that covers your supervised practice.","fact_ids":["sec01-F16","sec01-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Minors and adults","fact_ids":["sec01-F17","sec01-F18","sec01-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Under eighteen: test inside driver education.","fact_ids":["sec01-F17","sec01-F18","sec01-R07"]},{"text":"Home-schooled: information sheet HS three.","fact_ids":["sec01-F17","sec01-F18","sec01-R07"]},{"text":"Eighteen or older: sixty-day permit hold or approved course.","fact_ids":["sec01-F17","sec01-F18","sec01-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Where you take the road test depends on your age. Applicants under eighteen take the road skills test inside their driver education course, at a public, private or commercial school, while home-schooled applicants follow information sheet HS three. At eighteen or older, you must hold the learner permit for sixty days before the first road test, or finish approved driver education. The school tests driver education students, while DMV staff test permit holders. So minors take the road test inside their driver education course, while adults choose between a sixty-day permit hold with DMV testing, or an approved course with school testing.","fact_ids":["sec01-F17","sec01-F18","sec01-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec01-u03-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Do not mix the waits","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08","sec01-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Road test: one attempt per business day.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"One failure: wait two days.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08","sec01-F06"]},{"text":"Three DMV failures: in-vehicle training first.","fact_ids":["sec01-F19","sec01-R08","sec01-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap: the road test retake rules are not the knowledge exam rules. The road test allows one attempt per business day. After a failure, you wait two days.
